destination.name: Ararat
destination.tagline: Gateway to the Grampians with gold-rush, Chinese and asylum history
destination.description: Ararat is about 200 km north-west of Melbourne on the Western Highway and is known as the Gateway to the Grampians. Gold found in 1857 made it a boomtown, and it is the only city in Australia founded by Chinese people, a story told at the Gum San Chinese Heritage Centre. Visitors can tour J Ward, the former home of the criminally insane, and the Aradale asylum. Seppelt at Great Western, a short drive away, has 3 km of 1800s tunnels, the largest underground cellar in the Southern Hemisphere.
whyVisit: Taste wine at nearby cellar doors

goodToKnow.title: Train from Melbourne
goodToKnow.detail: V/Line runs trains from Southern Cross several times daily, and The Overland to Adelaide stops twice a week.

goodToKnow.title: Book cellar tours
goodToKnow.detail: Seppelt's tunnel tours run at set times, listed as 11am, 1pm and 3pm, for a fee, so check times before driving out.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Mild {months} weather suits touring wineries and heritage sites.

notes: Best months derived from climate (warm summers with cold fronts, cool rainy winters), not a recommendation from a source. Tunnel tour times should be re-checked.
